description: God tells them to stop saying 'prophecy from the Lord' when they are really giving authority to their own ideas. Putting His name on our own hopes is easier to do than we think.
excerpt: Because my emotions and feelings had lied to me. What I thought was a clear word from the Lord turned out to be my own hopes wearing a spiritual label.
verse: "You should keep asking each other, 'What is the Lord's answer?' or 'What is the Lord saying?' But stop using this phrase, 'prophecy from the Lord.' For people are using it to give authority to their own ideas, turning upside down the words of our God, the living God, the Lord of Heaven's Armies."
body_html:
I've had people say "God said" to me a lot over the years.

Most meant well and really believed they were hearing from Him. But even from a young age I started to realize that even the best-intentioned person could be wrong. And adding God's name to something you think or feel makes it worse, because now you're putting words in His mouth.

I say that as someone who did it.

When I got engaged in my early 20's, I told people I knew God said I was supposed to marry this guy. I really believed it. I really felt it. My emotions were all in. My prayer time had confirmed it in my heart. I was convinced it was from the Lord.

And I didn't end up marrying him.

That whole experience changed the way I talk about hearing from God. Because my emotions and feelings had lied to me. What I thought was a clear word from the Lord turned out to be my own hopes wearing a spiritual label. If I had been more careful with my words, I wouldn't have put God's name on something that wasn't from Him.

Since then, I've made a rule for myself. I don't say "God said" unless I'm sharing a truth that's actually in the Bible. If God said it in Scripture, I can say He said it. If it's just something I'm sensing or feeling or wrestling with, I say that instead. I feel like. I don't know for sure if God is saying this, but I feel strongly. I've been praying about this and I think.

Those phrases feel weaker, but they're more honest. And honesty is what God is after here.

The false prophets in Jeremiah's day were doing the same thing I did when I was engaged, just on a bigger scale. Taking their own ideas and slapping God's name on them to give them weight. And God says to stop it. Stop using that phrase to give authority to your own thoughts. Ask real questions instead. What is God actually saying? What is His answer?

That's a humbler posture. It leaves room for the possibility that we might be wrong. It keeps God's name out of things that aren't from Him. And it invites actual seeking instead of assuming.

I want to be careful with His name. He's the living God. His words matter. Mine don't carry the same weight, and I shouldn't pretend they do.

Are you careful with how you use the phrase "God said," or has it become a way to give weight to what you already wanted to be true?
question: Are you careful with how you use the phrase "God said," or has it become a way to give weight to what you already wanted to be true?
